hospitals.description: Yale New Haven Children's Hospital is the pediatric arm of Yale New Haven Hospital and the main academic children's hospital for southern Connecticut, taught by Yale School of Medicine faculty. Its New Haven building sits on Park Street at the edge of the York Street medical campus, a short walk from Yale's downtown and the Hill neighborhood. The hospital runs a 21 bed PICU that includes the state's only dedicated six bed pediatric cardiac ICU, two NICU floors rated Level IV, inpatient child and adolescent psychiatry, and a 24 hour Level I pediatric trauma emergency department. It also operates a second inpatient campus inside Bridgeport Hospital and supplies pediatric hospitalist and emergency coverage to Greenwich Hospital and other Yale New Haven Health sites, so its APP teams reach well beyond New Haven. A 24/7 critical care transport team with ground and air options brings infants and children in from across the region.
highlights: Ranked #1 children's hospital in Connecticut and #2 in New England by U.S. News 2025-26
208 licensed beds across New Haven and the Bridgeport campus
21 bed PICU including the only dedicated pediatric cardiac ICU in Connecticut (6 beds)
Level IV NICU (AAP, 2018) on two floors of the children's hospital
Level I pediatric trauma center with 24 hour pediatric emergency department
Yale pediatric hospitalists also staff Bridgeport, Greenwich and Griffin newborn and inpatient services
Yale New Haven Hospital campuses are ANCC Magnet designated
hospitals.notes: Bed counts differ: Wikipedia lists 202 beds and a 19 bed PICU; the 2025 YNHHS ranking release says 208 licensed beds and the YNHH critical care page says 21 PICU beds (including the 6 bed PCICU). The 208 likely includes the 42 beds licensed to YNHCH at Bridgeport Hospital, which has its own record. Postings for both campuses appear on jobs.ynhhs.org under Yale New Haven Hospital or Bridgeport Hospital. New Haven is about 2 hours from Boston and 1.5 to 2 hours from New York City by train (Metro-North and Amtrak at Union Station).

hospitals.description: Connecticut Children's is the state's only freestanding children's hospital, an eight story building on Washington Street in Hartford that opened in 1996 next to the Hartford Hospital campus. It grew out of the Newington Children's Hospital, which began in 1898, and today serves as the primary pediatric teaching hospital for UConn and Quinnipiac medical schools. The main campus holds an 18 bed PICU, a Level I pediatric trauma center and emergency department, and a 24/7 neonatal and pediatric critical care transport team. Its neonatology program runs the Level IV NICU inside Hartford Hospital and the Level III NICU at UConn Health in Farmington, and its physicians cover nurseries and pediatric units at a ring of affiliate hospitals, so many APRN roles are posted under Connecticut Children's even when the work is on another campus. Hartford is a mid sized capital city with easy access to the suburbs of the Farmington Valley and West Hartford.
highlights: Only freestanding children's hospital in Connecticut

Runs a 32 bed Level IV NICU at Hartford Hospital and a Level III NICU at UConn Health

The NICU at Hartford Hospital and the NICU at UConn Health have their own records here because they sit in those hospitals.

Barnum as its first board president, is a 501 bed Yale affiliated teaching hospital and Level II trauma center that also houses the second inpatient campus of Yale New Haven Children's Hospital.
